summary.scope: Four exact atan/asin-acos/commuted-atan/pi identities at four coefficient widths, cold and numerically warmed requests, three exact perturbations and four allowances. Each definitive sign agrees with the exact identity; unlimited retry certifies it and a later zero-budget query retains the proof. Python Fraction and Rug independently check each numerical observation against the exact rational perturbation. A finite public/serialized corpus, not an allocation/time proof.

New budgeted APIs on 48 symbolic angle fixtures with nine finite non-rational residuals, four trig families and serialized/public controls. Includes sqrt(2), ln(2), exp(1), atan(1/2), sqrt(2)-1, signed/scaled sqrt(2), and exp(100); lattice/non-lattice periodic coefficients, nearby poles, factored/distributed arithmetic, cancelled extreme offsets and 64 offset wrappers. Four-query schedule shares one allowance of one million work units. A prior zero-unit request is typed or reuses an already available constructor cache; a later zero-unit request must reuse the completed cache and retain every established sign. All returned samples are independently enclosed. Directed 1024-bit MPFR pi and residual enclosures feed exact derivative-one sin/cos intervals and exact quotient bounds. Each process is capped at 192 MiB, CPU 2/3 seconds and wall 4 seconds. Scoped evidence, not an exhaustive proof or matched benchmark.

24 exact principal-root product identities, including reciprocal forms and 64/256/1024-bit rational factors, three exact perturbations and four allowances. Numerical warmup precedes the explicit shared allowance. Independent rational oracles check both approximations; every definite sign must agree, and an unlimited retry must certify and retain the result at zero budget. This is a scoped accounting/certificate replay, not a wall-time or memory proof.

12 additional cube/fourth-root product identities with 64/256/1024-bit rational factors and reciprocal forms, three exact perturbations and four allowances. A 65536-bit numerical warmup precedes the explicit shared allowance; the larger precision floor retains conservative field-degree proofs when the 4096-bit dependency search declines. Independent rational oracles check both approximations; every definite sign must agree, and an unlimited retry must certify and retain the result at zero budget. This is a scoped accounting/certificate replay, not a wall-time or memory proof.

Four exact polynomial/surd-inverse/rational/opaque-atom identities at four coefficient widths, cold and numerically warmed requests, three exact perturbations and four allowances. Each definitive sign agrees with the exact identity; unlimited retry certifies it and a later zero-budget query retains the proof. Python Fraction and Rug independently check each numerical observation against the exact rational perturbation. A finite public/serialized corpus, not an allocation/time proof.

Original scalar failure/control and curve-scope workloads. The curve scope can contain a typed scalar Err; its existing counters still do not bound scalar work. This is not admission of the prototype or a total resource guarantee.

summary.scope: Termination and typed-domain result-shape witnesses only. The zero trigonometric denominators follow exact pi-multiple identities; perturbed and inverse-function inputs are mathematically in domain. Successful finite samples are not credited with verified numerical accuracy. Independent enclosures and constructor-valid controls remain required for repair validation.

Four serialized private trig node families, exact-rational input matrix, ordinary constructor controls and repeated precision orders. Passing samples are checked against independent exact-rational alternating-series enclosures. This does not establish all private kernel ranges, exact poles, concurrency or aggregate work bounds.

Six serialized trig node families and equivalent public controls, sixteen signed exact dyadic inputs from 31.5 through 1048576, two initial precisions and four-query schedules. Directed 1024-bit MPFR sin/cos enclosures are converted to exact rationals; sinc/cosc bounds use exact rational division/subtraction. Each process is capped at 192 MiB, CPU 2/3 seconds and wall 4 seconds. This is scoped correctness/resource evidence, not an exhaustive range proof or a matched benchmark.

Exact half-pi lattice identities with symbolic binary offsets, cancellation, distributed rational coefficients and deep wrappers. Every returned one-unit interval must contain the exact integer oracle; poles require DivideByZero. Every process uses the unchanged 192 MiB, CPU 2/3-second, wall 4-second caps. This is scoped correctness/resource evidence, not exhaustive symbolic completeness or a benchmark.

57 symbolic angle fixtures, four trig families and serialized/public controls. Includes non-lattice multiples, finite residuals +/-1/1024 and +/-1000, nearby poles, factored/distributed arithmetic, signed multiples, cancelled extreme offsets, and 64 offset wrappers. Four-query cold/warm precision schedule; directed 1024-bit MPFR of independently reduced angles plus an exact derivative-one interval and exact quotient bounds. Each process is capped at 192 MiB, CPU 2/3 seconds and wall 4 seconds. Scoped correctness/resource evidence, not an exhaustive proof or matched benchmark.

48 symbolic angle fixtures with nine finite non-rational residuals, four trig families and serialized/public controls. Includes sqrt(2), ln(2), exp(1), atan(1/2), sqrt(2)-1, signed/scaled sqrt(2), and exp(100); lattice/non-lattice periodic coefficients, nearby poles, factored/distributed arithmetic, cancelled extreme offsets and 64 offset wrappers. Four-query cold/warm schedule. Directed 1024-bit MPFR pi and residual enclosures feed exact derivative-one sin/cos intervals and exact quotient bounds. Each process is capped at 192 MiB, CPU 2/3 seconds and wall 4 seconds. Scoped evidence, not an exhaustive proof or matched benchmark.

Public constructors for pi, sqrt(2) and sin(1/3), minus independently directed dyadic floors at 80 and 1100 bits, with both signs and optional serialization reconstruction. Twenty-four sequential schedules check coarse zero-work reuse, finer misses and unlimited retry; 24 prewarmed eight-thread schedules reuse an actually spent shared allowance; 72 mixed eight-thread schedules combine shared small allowances, a separate large allowance and unlimited refinement. Six invalid-domain controls cover four threads each. Every successful sample encloses both 2560-bit directed MPFR endpoints, also rechecked using Python Fraction. Every definite fact agrees with the oracle and each thread retains all previously observed sign/zero/magnitude facts. Original serialization bytes must remain unchanged.

Seven compositions use only ordinary public Computable constructors. Three directed-MPFR residual families at 80 and 1100 bits, both signs, exact-zero controls, shared-child or independently reconstructed roots, three query orders and six shared allowances cover 468 valid schedules. Each schedule records bounded calls, every root fact after each call, unlimited retries, zero-work cached samples, finer requests and retries. Fifty-four invalid-descendant schedules use the same seven compositions. The real identities provide each root oracle from independently directed 2560-bit base enclosures; Python Fraction independently checks numerical containment. The unchanged corpus is replayed against the unretained runtime extraction.

decision: Keep the exact runtime domain decisions and route them through the same pure BoundInfo method included by Verus. The extraction adds conditional proof coverage without losing any observed successful query, fact, work allowance or allocation behavior in the frozen deterministic corpora. The original-cap cost comparison and predeclared repeat pass. This is the new isolated baseline, not main runtime admission.
limits: The proof includes the actual production predicate body and establishes a real-domain consequence conditional on a valid incoming bound. Independent real existence, producer soundness, caller ordering, graph semantics and atomic publication remain separate obligations; all thirteen whole-crate groups remain open.

Ten acceptance/dependency tests and 226 rejected mutations plus four passing baselines do not satisfy the still-pending fixed pre-Verus acceptance report. The failed v1760 proof attempt and all earlier failed experiments remain immutable.

The nine broad commands cover scalar configurations and the five-crate consumer stack, not every workspace/CI job. Thirty-three ignored tests and fourteen inherited Cargo example-filename warnings remain; both strict Clippy configurations have zero warnings.

The 39 direct-binary caps and 648 public schedules retain 192 MiB, CPU 2/3-second and four-second wall limits. Numerical corpora preserve their individual original limits; the base and precision corpora use a three-second wall limit without the later CPU guard. The 78 private-kernel cases check result shapes, so 4129 is not a count of independent numerical oracle checks.

All deterministic observations remain identical, including samples, typed errors, work, facts and recorded allocations. Only duration fields and known executable phase paths are normalized. The 78 concurrent public cases compare setup/oracle/process contracts separately from schedule-dependent outcomes.

The public fact audit checks observed worker/root sequences and joined final snapshots. Thread stress is not exhaustive interleaving verification. Composed child snapshots start at the first serialized observation; the frozen Rust probe separately checks the initial child state. Exact-rational flags are checked for retention, not general recognition soundness.

The 1584 domain queries include 453 successes and 1131 Exhausted answers, unchanged from v1754. The zero-Rust-allocation observation applies to 56 private certificate queries. The 48 endpoint/invalid/upper-only controls, 36 fine-retry schedules and 144 cached retry queries remain unchanged; these are nested in the nine domain cap phases, not additional executable processes.

All 1566 fresh cost processes and 1098 separate CPU preludes pass their original caps. The initial 5.0501 percent pi increase and prescribed 1.0191 percent repeat both remain recorded. Seven local probe executables shrink 48-152 bytes. These measurements establish neither causal attribution, a uniform speedup nor whole-board performance/size parity.

The local cost baseline remains v1754. Older original-cap failures at v1638/v1710, the earlier retained integer-control tradeoff and the fixed pre-Verus acceptance baseline are not erased or reset by this successful comparison.

EvaluationBudget excludes aggregate bytes/time and unmetered algebraic helpers. Construction and structural inspection are outside the public query allowances. Reconstructed graphs discard sharing/caches while process-global constants may already be warm.

This retains an isolated candidate only. Main retains its original scalar failure and all 49 preexisting worktree entries. Native combination, full-board admission, all 39 properties, 14 targets and crate future work remain in scope; no property/target status changes and no push follow from this checkpoint.
